c.tagline: Russia's subtropical Black Sea resort, from palm-lined beaches to Olympic ski slopes.

taxi.fareNote: Most rides are booked through the Yandex Go app, which is cheap and reliable; street taxis are unmetered, so agree a price first. Note that foreign bank cards do not work in Russia - carry cash or a local card.

emergency.note: 112 is the unified emergency number (you can also dial 102 for police, 103 for ambulance, 101 for fire).

avoid.reason: Avoid crossing into nearby Abkhazia just south of Adler — a disputed territory with border restrictions and consular no-go status.
Watch for overcharging taxis, inflated beach-vendor and photo-with-animal scams along the seafront promenade in high summer.

hood_desc: The lively heart of the resort, with the seafront promenade, Riviera Park, the Winter Theatre, the Sochi Arboretum (Dendrarium), and the main shopping and dining; the walkable base for most first-time visitors.

The southern district by the airport and railway hub, home to the 2014 Olympic Park, Sochi Park theme park, the Imeretinskaya beachfront, and the newest resort hotels; great tourist infrastructure and family beaches.

The mountain resort town about 40 km inland, base for the Rosa Khutor, Gazprom, and Gorky Gorod ski areas that hosted the 2014 Winter Olympics; alpine hotels and cable cars, with skiing in winter and hiking in summer.
A quieter green district between central Sochi and Adler, known for its pebble beaches, subtropical parks, and the Tisosamshitovaya (yew-boxwood) grove; relaxed and residential.
A historic spa quarter famous for its sulfur-rich balneological baths, set in wooded hills just south of the center; a calm, wellness-focused retreat.
lodging: Park Inn by Radisson Rosa Khutor

water.note: Locals often boil tap water; visitors are safest with bottled.

transit.pay: City bus fares are paid on board by cash or (local) contactless card, roughly 40 rubles a ride; there is no separate smartcard. The Lastochka commuter trains run along the coast between central Sochi, Khosta, Adler, the airport, and up to Krasnaya Polyana, with tickets bought at stations or the RZD app.
transit.hours: City buses run roughly 6am to 11pm; Lastochka coastal trains run frequently through the day, with ride-hailing (Yandex Go) filling the late-night gap.
transit.note: Sochi has no metro or tram. The backbone is an extensive city bus network plus the Lastochka electric coastal trains that link the strung-out districts of Greater Sochi and climb to the mountain resorts at Krasnaya Polyana.

transit.m: Aeroexpress / Lastochka train to central Sochi, ~50 min
City bus to Adler and central Sochi, ~60 min

tip.r: Not obligatory; leaving around 10% at restaurants for good service is appreciated.
